question: Did California's AB 1228 minimum wage for workers at large limited-service restaurant chains ($20 per hour from 1 April 2024; signed 28 September 2023) change employment in California's limited-service restaurants (NAICS 722513) over its first eight quarters, 2024Q2-2026Q1, relative to limited-service restaurants in other states, and did the effect change between the first and the second year, when the policy's bite fell? The published QCEW-based studies disagree (Clemens, Edwards, Meer and Nguyen, NBER w34033 revised 2026: a decline of about 3.5%; Dube, NBER w35171, 2026: near zero). This is a pre-specified update of a contested question, not a new question: the latest published QCEW window ends in 2025Q4 (Clemens et al., w35931), so the data add one preliminary quarter, 2026Q1; the 2026Q2 release is due on 2 December 2026 and the crew does not wait for it.
hypotheses: H1 (first stage, in weekly earnings): the pooled 2024Q2-2026Q1 ATT on log average weekly wage (QCEW weekly earnings per job, not the hourly wage the law sets; fewer hours would bias it toward zero) of California NAICS 722513 relative to the comparison group, with the primary estimator fixed at the design gate, is positive: one-sided test at 5%. The inference method must be valid with a single treated state (Ferman-Pinto, conformal, or a permutation whose comparison pool is large enough that a 5% test is attainable without California ranking first by construction); standard errors clustered by state are not used. The run level-mde, after the design gate and before any run that reads post-2023Q3 outcomes, on data through 2019Q4 only, shows that the selected pool and method attain the stated level, as the design specifies. Reported also for each year separately, because the $20 fast-food wage did not rise in 2025 or 2026 while California's general minimum did (its premium fell from $4.00 to $3.10). If H1 fails, H2 is reported as uninformative about the wage floor.

H2 (main): the pooled 2024Q2-2026Q1 ATT on log employment of California NAICS 722513, same estimator and inference. Decision rule, fixed now, with b = 0.02 log points: compute the two-sided 95% CI [L, U] and the 90% CI [l, u] (a two one-sided test at 5%) with the H1 inference method. Sign: 'negative' if U < 0, 'positive' if L > 0, else 'sign undetermined'. Size: 'smaller than b' if -b < l and u < b, 'at least b' if u < -b or l > b, else 'size undetermined'. The headline label is the pair, in this exhaustive and mutually exclusive table: (negative, at least b) = 'decline of at least 2%'; (negative, smaller than b) = 'decline smaller than 2%'; (negative, size undetermined) = 'decline, size not distinguishable from 2%'; (sign undetermined, smaller than b) = 'no effect as large as 2%'; (sign undetermined, at least b) = 'inconclusive'; (sign undetermined, size undetermined) = 'inconclusive'; and the positive cases symmetrically ('increase of at least 2%', 'increase smaller than 2%', 'increase, size not distinguishable from 2%'). The bound: with a pooled weekly-wage effect of about 7% (Dube 2026, Table 1 Panel A, SDID; a close but not identical estimand: 2024Q2-2025Q3 against a 2023Q4 base, employment per capita), -0.02 corresponds to an own-wage elasticity of about -0.29, the least negative of the elasticities Clemens et al. report, and the QCEW estimates Clemens et al. report (about -2.3% to -3.9%) lie beyond -2% (their one-year QWI medians, near -1.4%, do not); a CI inside +/-0.02 therefore excludes the Clemens et al. QCEW reading, and a CI wholly below -0.02 excludes Dube's. The run level-mde (after the design gate, before any run that reads post-2023Q3 outcomes, on data through 2019Q4 only) computes the minimum detectable effect at 80% power and the other power quantities the design lists, and the paper reports them next to H2. Timing for H1-H3, fixed now: the base period is 2023Q3, the last quarter before AB 1228 was signed (2022Q3-2023Q3 is not policy-free: AB 257, enacted September 2022 and stayed in January 2023, would have allowed a fast-food wage of up to $22; the design reports a pre-AB 257 base as a robustness check); 2023Q4 and 2024Q1 (between signing and the effective date) enter neither the base nor the pooled post-period and are reported separately as a report-only anticipation estimate, as Sosinskiy and Reich (2026, Table A3) already report them; Dube (2026, Table 1 Panel B), whose base is the 2022Q1-2023Q3 mean so that 2023Q4 stays out of it, is the published result closest to this timing and is named as such in the paper; Dube's 2023Q4 base is a pre-specified robustness check, not an alternative primary. Choice of the primary specification, fixed now because the published literature already maps each choice to its result (w35931; Dube 2026, Table D1) and the PI has read that map: the design gate does not pick the estimator, detrending, outcome normalization, comparison pool or fitting window by judgement. The Designer lists a candidate set covering both published approaches (at least: DD and DD with a state-specific linear trend fitted on the pre-period, each on log employment and on log employment per capita; synthetic control; SDID; with the comparison pools both studies use), and the primary is the candidate with the smallest root mean squared error of placebo-in-time pooled ATTs at pseudo-treatment dates that use only data before 2023Q3 (the pseudo-dates, their windows and the tie-break are fixed in the design). Two named secondary analyses are reported whatever the rule picks: Clemens et al.'s detrended indexed DD and Dube's SDID, both re-estimated with the 2023Q3 timing above. The study is therefore pre-specified but not blind, and the paper says so.

H3 (reduced-form year two minus year one): the ATT on log employment for 2025Q2-2026Q1 minus that for 2024Q2-2025Q1, same estimator and inference, reported next to the yearly H1 wage effects (and the implied yearly own-wage elasticities), because the policy's bite fell in year two and a change cannot be attributed to time alone. 'Larger decline in year two' if the 95% CI of the difference is below 0, 'smaller decline in year two' if above 0, otherwise 'no detectable change'. If the pre-period MDE of the difference exceeds 0.04 (twice b), H3 is reported as uninformative whatever the estimate.
contribution: A pre-specified (not blind) update with modest novelty, stated as such: the estimand, base period, a rule that picks the primary estimator from pre-2023Q3 data only, inference valid with a single treated state and decision rules are fixed and reviewed before any post-2023Q3 outcome is computed; H2 adds an equivalence test against a 2% bound that separates the two published readings; H3 compares year two with year one next to the yearly wage effects, because the fast-food premium over California's general minimum fell from $4.00 to $3.10; the data add one preliminary quarter (2026Q1) to the latest published window (2025Q4). Decompositions of the published disagreement (Dube 2026, Tables D1-D2; Clemens et al. w35931, Table A1; Sosinskiy and Reich 2026, Appendix A) and published anticipation and base-period checks (Dube 2026, Table 1 Panel B; Sosinskiy and Reich 2026, Table A3; w35931, footnote 5) are cited, not repeated as findings. The PI and the Scout know the published estimates and a published descriptive California-vs-rest-of-US index for 722513 through March 2026 (Recording Law data page, 6 November 2026; the PI read its two March 2026 values in the Scout's report) (disclosed); the analysing roles compute nothing on post-period outcomes before the design gate. Limits known now: QCEW counts jobs and weekly earnings, not hours or hourly wages; part of NAICS 722513 is outside the law's coverage (Melo et al. 2026 put covered-chain employment about one-third below QCEW 722513 in California in 2025, so roughly two-thirds is covered), so effects on covered jobs are diluted; covered chains are also coded in NAICS 722515 and 722511 (Melo et al.), so neither is a clean control; county cells are suppressed more often from 2025, so the design must say whether the analysis is at state or county level; 2026Q1 is preliminary and will be revised.

design.summary: State-level comparison of California's private NAICS 722513 employment (quarterly mean of the three monthly QCEW levels, seasonally adjusted with fixed 2014-2019 state factors) with donor states over 2024Q2-2026Q1 relative to the base quarter 2023Q3. 2023Q4-2024Q1 is held out as a report-only anticipation window, and 2020Q1-2021Q4 is excluded from every fitting window. The primary estimator and pool are not chosen by judgement. One logged analysis run reads only a panel truncated at 2019Q4. It picks the candidate with the smallest root mean squared error of California's placebo pooled ATTs on log employment at six pre-COVID pseudo-treatment dates (2016Q1-2017Q2). The 24 candidates are: DD and pre-trend-adjusted DD, each with CEM-style aggregate or Dube-style population weights; demeaned synthetic control; and synthetic DID. Each is fitted on log employment or log employment per capita, with Dube's 20 federal-minimum states or with all 50 other states and DC. Inference is a placebo t-test whose SE is the larger of the population-scaled (Ferman-Pinto as implemented by Dube) and the unscaled placebo SE, which is conservative for California, the largest unit, whatever the mix of size-related and state-level noise. Its critical values are the more conservative of t_J and the quantiles of placebo tests on the ten most populous federal-minimum (D20) states at pre-COVID pseudo-dates; this is computed in level-mde, after the design gate and before any post-2023Q3 outcome is read, on data ending 2019Q4. H1 (log weekly wage), H2 (sign x size rule, b = 0.02) and H3 (year two minus year one) then use the selected estimator and pool. Both camps' specifications (CEM detrended indexed DD, Dube SDID) are named secondaries; their labels are reported next to the primary's in the abstract, and the headline is stated as not robust to either if its sign category differs. Pre-specified robustness and placebo checks (Dube's 2023Q4 base, a pre-AB 257 2022Q2 base, the other pool, NAICS 7225, the final-data window, non-722513 employment, NAICS 722511) are reported whatever they show.
design.estimand: tau = (1/8) * sum over t in 2024Q2..2026Q1 of [Y_CA,t(1) - Y_CA,t(0)] - [Y_CA,2023Q3(1) - Y_CA,2023Q3(0)], where Y is seasonally adjusted log employment (quarterly mean of the three monthly levels) of private NAICS 722513 establishments in California and Y(0) is the path without AB 1228. If AB 1228 had no effect before its signing (28 September 2023, after the September pay period), the second bracket is zero. tau is an intent-to-treat effect on the whole industry code, covered and uncovered establishments together, and in log points (reported also as 100*(exp(tau)-1) percent and as jobs). H1: the same with log average weekly wage. H3: tau_2 - tau_1, with year 1 = 2024Q2-2025Q1 and year 2 = 2025Q2-2026Q1. Candidates on log(employment/population) estimate the same tau, under the maintained assumption that AB 1228 did not change California's resident population; this is why the selection rule can compare all candidates on one scale (F16).
design.identifying_assumption: Without AB 1228, California's seasonally adjusted log 722513 employment (H1: log weekly wage) after 2023Q3 would have stayed as far from the selected counterfactual as it was before. For DD candidates the reference is the 2023Q3 gap, with the pre-period gap trend extrapolated for the trend variant. For synthetic control the reference is the pre-period mean gap; for SDID it is the time-weighted pre-period gap. The rule's premise is that the candidate that reproduced California's actual path best at pre-COVID pseudo-dates is the one for which this holds best. That path includes California's own general minimum-wage phase-in (July 2014 to $15 in 2022; Wiltshire et al., notes section 10), which is part of Y(0) for AB 1228; so the premise is fit to California's path under its own general-MW ramp, and it assumes that whatever lets a candidate track that ramp in 2016-2019 (a gap trend, or R50 donors with their own increases) still tracks California's AB 1228-free path in 2024-2026, when the general minimum rose more slowly (T17). The data would contradict the assumption if: (i) the selected candidate's placebo RMSE is near or above b = 0.02 (reported by select); (ii) the event path shows systematic gaps over 2022Q1-2023Q3 (event-path); (iii) employment outside 722513 shows an effect (plc-nonff); or (iv) the estimate moves materially with the base (rob-base-2023q4, rob-pre-ab257) or with the pool (rob-pool). None of these checks can confirm the assumption.
design.method: SOFTWARE: Python 3.14.6, numpy 2.5.3, scipy 1.18.1, pandas 3.0.5, statsmodels 0.15.0. Code/requirements.txt is frozen from a fresh venv; StatsPAI 1.43.0 may be used only as a cross-check in check-methods, never in a run that produces a claim. Nothing in a study run is random (the check-methods Monte Carlo uses numpy default_rng(20261121)). Weights are solved by scipy.optimize.minimize (SLSQP, simplex constraints, start at uniform weights, ftol 1e-12, maxiter 2000); the tests check the KKT conditions to 1e-6. NOTATION: B is the base quarter: 2023Q3 for the real analysis, B' for a pseudo-date. COVID quarters C = 2020Q1-2021Q4 (Dube's exclusion) are never used in any fit, base, trend or SE calculation. Fit window F(B) = all quarters from 2014Q1 to B that are not in C. Anticipation window A(B) = {B+1, B+2}. Post window P(B) = B+3..B+10 (8 quarters); year 1 = B+3..B+6; year 2 = B+7..B+10. For the real B these are F = 2014Q1-2019Q4 plus 2022Q1-2023Q3 (31 quarters), A = 2023Q4-2024Q1 and P = 2024Q2-2026Q1. Time t is the calendar quarter index, so the COVID gap counts as elapsed time in trends. OUTCOMES (per state and per donor aggregate; seasonal adjustment is applied to every series that enters an estimator, after aggregation): E = ln(mean of month1-3 employment); P = SA ln(employment) - ln(population); W = ln(avg_wkly_wage) as BLS publishes it (aggregates: ln(sum of total_qtrly_wages / (13 * sum of mean employment))). SEASONAL ADJUSTMENT, fixed and the same for every run: 2x4 centred moving average m_t = (0.5y_{t-2} + y_{t-1} + y_t + y_{t+1} + 0.5y_{t+2})/4 for t = 2014Q3..2019Q2 (it uses only 2014Q1-2019Q4). The factor s_q is the mean of y_t - m_t over the five quarters of type q, minus the mean of the four s_q. The adjusted series is y_t - s_q(t) for all t. ESTIMATORS (closed forms; g_t = Y_CA,t - Ybar_donor,t): DD: tau = mean_{t in P} g_t - g_B. DDT (CEM-style detrended DD): tau = mean_{t in P} [g_t - g_B - b(t - B)], where b is the OLS slope of g_t on t over the calendar quarters B-8..B that are not in C. For the real B that is 2022Q1-2023Q3 (7 points); for pseudo-dates, 9 points. Equivalent to state-specific linear trends in the weighted 2x2 comparison. Donor average for DD and DDT, two weightings: AGG (CEM): the donor aggregate series, i.e. summed employment, summed population and summed wages, logged. POPW (Dube): population-weighted mean of donor log series, weights pop_j at B. SC (demeaned synthetic control, Doudchenko-Imbens / Ferman-Pinto): simplex weights w minimising sum over F of [(Y_CA,t - Ybar_CA,F) - sum_j w_j (Y_j,t - Ybar_j,F)]^2; tau = mean over P of the same demeaned gap. The demeaned form is needed because California's log employment level lies outside the donors' convex hull. SDID (Arkhangelsky et al. 2021, Algorithm 1, no sparsification): the unit weights (omega0, omega in the simplex) minimise sum over F of (omega0 + sum_j omega_j Y_jt - Y_CA,t)^2 + zeta^2 |F| ||omega||^2. Here zeta = (1 * 8)^(1/4) * sigma_hat, and sigma_hat is computed as Arkhangelsky et al. (2021) eq. (2.2): sigma_hat^2 = sum over donors j and over the pairs of consecutive calendar quarters (t, t+1) both in F of (Delta_jt - Delta_bar)^2, divided by J times the number of such pairs, where Delta_jt = Y_j,t+1 - Y_j,t and Delta_bar is their mean over the same donors and pairs (with no gap this is N_co (T_pre - 1)). The time weights (lambda0, lambda in the simplex) minimise sum_j (lambda0 + sum_{s in F} lambda_s Y_js - mean_{t in window} Y_jt)^2 + (1e-6 sigma_hat)^2 J ||lambda||^2 (the paper's zeta^2 N_co ||lambda||^2 with zeta = 1e-6 sigma_hat, fn 3; N_co = J donors). tau = (mean_window Y_CA - sum_s lambda_s Y_CA,s) - sum_j omega_j (mean_window Y_j - sum_s lambda_s Y_js). omega and zeta are fitted once with the 8-quarter post window and reused for the year windows and the anticipation window; lambda is refitted for each window. For W (H1), each estimator is re-applied to the wage series with the same pool: weights refitted on wages for SC/SDID, the gap trend fitted on wages for DDT, and the same weighting for DD/DDT (F16: H1 uses the selected estimator and pool with log weekly wage as outcome). Dube's reuse of employment weights appears in S2 and in the denominator of the own-wage elasticities (DECISIONS; design-r1 D5). CANDIDATE SET (24, in this order, which is also the last tie-break): for e in [DD, DDT], w in [AGG, POPW], n in [E, P], pool in [D20, R50]: 16 candidates. Then SC x [E, P] x [D20, R50] and SDID x [E, P] x [D20, R50]: 8. Ids look like 'DDT-POPW-P-D20'. SELECTION RULE (run select; input data/derived/state_panel_pre.csv, 2014Q1-2019Q4 only; the single cutoff for the selection, the level check and the MDE is 2019Q4. That is earlier than both 'before 2023Q3' (H2 rule) and 'pre-2023Q4' (H2 MDE), and earlier than AB 257's enactment in September 2022 (literature-r1 L1)): pseudo-dates B' in {2016Q1, 2016Q2, 2016Q3, 2016Q4, 2017Q1, 2017Q2}, California treated, the candidate's pool as donors, windows F(B'), A(B'), P(B') as above, so every pseudo-window ends by 2019Q4 and contains no COVID quarter. B' starts at 2016Q1 because DDT needs B'-8 >= 2014Q1, and stops at 2017Q2 because B'+10 <= 2019Q4. The pseudo-ATT is tau_c(B') in log points; for P candidates it is read on the log-employment scale (F16). It is a fit error relative to California's AB 1228-free path, not an estimate of a zero policy effect: California's 2016-2019 path contains its general minimum-wage ramp, which the donors (D20 entirely, R50 partly) lack, so the rule favours candidates that track that ramp (design-r1 D3; T17). RMSE_c = sqrt(mean over the six B' of tau_c(B')^2). Primary = argmin RMSE_c. Tie-break: RMSEs equal after rounding to 4 decimals, then smaller max |tau_c(B')|, then the earlier candidate in the order above. The rule's parameters were fixed by the Designer on 2026-11-21 without computing any placebo or any statistic of the outcomes; no alternative set of pseudo-dates is computed by anyone (F15a). INFERENCE (H1-H3, anticip, S1, S2, robustness and placebo runs; valid with one treated state; no clustered SEs; design-r1 D1): for a statistic tau_u of treated unit u (u = California in every post-period run), compute the placebo estimate tau_j for each donor j in u's donor set (J donors), treating j as treated with the other J-1 donors (u excluded) and the same estimator, windows and outcome. Two SEs. Scaled: SE_s = sqrt((1/J) sum_j tau_j^2 pop_j(B)/pop_u(B)) (Dube's Ferman-Pinto scaling). Unscaled: SE_n = sqrt((1/J) sum_j tau_j^2). SE = max(SE_s, SE_n). Reason: if var(tau_j) = A + B/pop_j with A, B >= 0 (Ferman-Pinto's var(W_j|M_j) = A + B/M_j; the scaled SE alone imposes A = 0), then E[SE_s^2] = A mean_j(pop_j)/pop_u + B/pop_u and E[SE_n^2] = A + B mean_j(1/pop_j), against the truth A + B/pop_u. For California, larger than every donor, SE_s is at or below the truth and SE_n at or above it for every A, B >= 0, so the max is conservative for California itself, whatever the mix of state-level shocks (A) and size-related noise (B). It is not shown conservative if the variance rises with size (B < 0); the level check on large units is the check for that. Diagnostic, reported and never used for a decision: Ferman-Pinto's own step 3, OLS of tau_j^2 on 1 and 1/pop_j over the J placebos, giving A_hat, B_hat and SE_FP = sqrt(max(0, A_hat + B_hat/pop_u)). Critical values c_hi(p), c_lo(p) come from LEVEL CHECK below; each is at least as far from 0 as the t_J quantile. Two-sided 95% CI = [tau - c_hi(0.975) SE, tau - c_lo(0.025) SE]; 90% CI = [tau - c_hi(0.95) SE, tau - c_lo(0.05) SE]; the one-sided 5% test (H1) rejects if tau/SE > c_hi(0.95). P-values from t_J are reported for information; every label uses the CIs. A 5% test is attainable without California ranking first among the placebos (with D20, J = 20; with R50, J = 50; rob-7225 lists its own J). LEVEL CHECK (run level-mde; truncated input state_panel_pre.csv only; after the design gate and before any run that reads a post-2023Q3 outcome; design-r1 D1-D3): statistics checked: for the selected candidate, pooled W (H1), pooled E-or-P (H2) and the year-2-minus-year-1 difference (H3); the pooled H2 statistic of S1 and of S2 at the same pseudo-dates (S1: AGG, E, R50, endpoint trend (g_B' - g_B'-8)/8; S2: SDID, P, D20, fit window 2015Q1..B'); and the pooled H2 statistic of the selected estimator and outcome with the other pool (for rob-pool). At each of the six pseudo-dates B', for each unit u in the pool plus California, INFERENCE is applied with u treated and donors D_u = (pool minus u) plus California (California itself uses the pool), so the donor count stays J; T_u = tau_u/SE_u. For each statistic, and separately with SE, SE_s and SE_n, level-mde reports the empirical rates of T > t_{J,0.95}, T < -t_{J,0.95} and |T| > t_{J,0.975}: (i) over all 6(J+1) tests; (ii) by population tercile of the J+1 units at B'; (iii) over the decision set L; (iv) for California's six tests, with the diagnostic k = RMS of California's six T values. DECISION SET L (D1, D3): the ten most populous D20 states at each B' (60 tests). They are the large units among the states whose binding minimum was the federal $7.25 throughout 2014-2019 (verified by task s-mw-history), so their pseudo-ATTs have no own-policy content, unlike California's and many R50 states'. L contains no unit as large as California, so it can detect over-rejection that grows with size but cannot measure California's own level; that is what the max SE is for. EFFECTIVE DRAWS (D2): the six post windows (2016Q4-2018Q3 to 2018Q1-2019Q4) overlap by 3 to 7 of 8 quarters, so one unit's six tests are about two independent draws: about 2(J+1) independent draws over all tests (42 for D20, 102 for R50) and about 20 in L. CRITICAL VALUES (D2; no threshold and no choice between variants): for each statistic, c_hi(p) = max(t_{J,p}, empirical p-quantile of its 60 T values in L, numpy method 'higher') for p in {0.95, 0.975}, and c_lo(p) = min(-t_{J,1-p}, empirical p-quantile, method 'lower') for p in {0.025, 0.05}. With 60 values the 0.025 and 0.975 quantiles are the second smallest and second largest: attainable, but noisy with about 20 independent draws; that noise can only widen an interval relative to t_J, never narrow it. Use: the selected candidate's H1, H2 and H3 values apply to h1-wage, h2-emp, h3-years and the corresponding anticip statistics; S1's to sec-cemn; S2's to sec-dube; the other-pool value to rob-pool; the selected candidate's H2 value, with t at each run's own J, to the other robustness and placebo runs and to event-path bands. The rates are reported against 0.05 with a binomial band on the effective draws; they are evidence, not a switch. The design gate therefore approves a rule whose winner is unknown together with an inference procedure fixed for any winner; its empirical level is documented by level-mde before any post-2023Q3 outcome is read (F15b). MDE AND POWER (level-mde; design-r1 D6): SE_pre = sqrt(mean over B' of SE_CA(B')^2) for each statistic, with SE = max(SE_s, SE_n); SE_s,pre and SE_n,pre are reported too. MDE at 80% power: MDE_h2 = (c_hi(0.975) + t_{J,0.80}) SE_pre, MDE_h3 likewise, MDE_h1 = (c_hi(0.95) + t_{J,0.80}) SE_pre (one-sided). For H2's size label, an equivalence statement: h90 = max(c_hi(0.95), -c_lo(0.05)) SE_pre, the 90% CI half-width, reported against b = 0.02 ('no effect as large as 2%' is reachable only if h90 < b); and the probability of each of the nine H2 labels under tau = 0 and under tau = -0.035, computed from tau_hat = tau + SE_pre T with T ~ t_J and the CI rule above (closed form from the t_J cdf; no simulation). MDE_h2, h90 and the label probabilities are reported next to H2. If MDE_h3 > 0.04, H3 is reported as uninformative whatever its estimate. SE_pre rests on 2014-2019 noise and on seasonal factors fitted on the same years (T7, T13), so it is a lower bound: h2-emp and h3-years report MDE_h2, h90 and MDE_h3 recomputed with the real post-period SE next to the level-mde values (report-only; the H3 uninformative rule uses the larger of the two MDE_h3 values). DECISIONS (verdict run; exactly the approved rules): H1 supported if the pooled W statistic rejects the one-sided 5% test. If not, H2 is reported as uninformative about the wage floor. H2: sign from the 95% CI [L, U], size from the 90% CI [l, u] against b = 0.02, and the label from the nine-cell table in hypotheses[1]. H3: 95% CI of tau_2 - tau_1 below 0 means 'larger decline in year two', above 0 means 'smaller decline in year two', otherwise 'no detectable change'. Own-wage elasticities (pooled and yearly; design-r1 D5) = employment ATT / wage ATT, where the wage ATT in the denominator re-applies the selected candidate to log weekly wage with the employment fit reused (SC: the employment w; SDID: the employment omega and, per window, the employment lambda; DD and DDT have no fitted weights, so their H1 wage ATT is already this one, with the DDT trend fitted on wages). Numerator and denominator then use one comparison, which is what makes dilution by uncovered establishments roughly cancel, and it matches the reused-weights wage effect on which the -0.29 elasticity behind b was calibrated. For SC and SDID the ratio with the H1 (refitted) wage ATT is reported next to it, marked 'refitted wage weights'. An elasticity is computed only for windows whose H1 wage effect rejects the one-sided 5% test and whose reused-weights wage ATT is positive, otherwise 'not computed'. Point values only. MULTIPLE TESTING: no family-wise correction. H2 is the single primary employment test, H1 is a gate for reading it, and H3 is a separately labelled secondary with its own MDE rule. Secondaries, robustness checks and placebos are reported with CIs and rule labels marked 'not the headline'; they never create a new finding, but S1, S2 and runs 9, 10, 11 and 13 can qualify the headline (verdict; design-r1 D4). The paper says that with two placebo outcomes a chance 'failure' of one at 95% has probability of about 0.10. ORDER AFTER THE GATE: select, then level-mde, then any run that reads post-2023Q3 outcomes. Each post-period script declares runs/select/metrics.json and runs/level-mde/metrics.json as --input and takes the candidate and inference variant from them; nothing is hard-coded. select is run once. If a reviewed bug fix forces a rerun with --replace, the superseded record stays under runs/.superseded and the paper reports every selection run and its winner.
design.data: SOURCES: (1) BLS QCEW open-data industry slices, 2014Q1-2026Q1, vintage pinned by the manifest hashes (dr-fetch; data/CODEBOOK.md). Used: state rows (agglvl 58 for 722513 and 722511, 56 for 7225, 50 for industry 10) of NAICS 722513 private (own 5), 722511 private, 7225 private, and 10 Total Covered (own 0). County rows are not used: suppression of county restaurant cells jumps in 2025 in most states (CODEBOOK), so a county panel would be selected partly on post-period disclosure. No 722513 or 722511 state row is suppressed, and state totals include suppressed county data. (2) U.S. Census Bureau Population Estimates Program, July 1 resident population by state. 2013-2019 come from the 2010-2020 intercensal file sc-est2020int-alldata6.csv (SEX 0, ORIGIN 0, summed over RACE and AGE); 2020-2025 come from Vintage 2025 NST-EST2025-ALLDATA.csv (POPESTIMATE2020-2025). Both are in www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/popest/datasets/ (directory listings checked 2026-11-21) and are public domain. ln pop is interpolated linearly between July 1 anchors (placed at year + 0.5), with quarter q of year y placed at y + (q - 0.5)/4, and extrapolated after 2025.5 with the 2024-2025 log growth (2025Q3, 2025Q4 and 2026Q1 flagged, pop_extrap = 1; 2025Q3 sits at 2025.625, after the last anchor; CODEBOOK discrepancy 1). (3) For code checks only: synthdid package data california_prop99.csv (github.com/synth-inference/synthdid, data/, pinned at commit 70c1ce3eac58e28c30b67435ca377bb48baa9b8a; semicolon-delimited, columns State;Year;PacksPerCapita;treated, 39 states x 31 years; license: the package's 'GPL (>= 2) | BSD_3_clause + file LICENSE', covering its redistribution of Abadie, Diamond and Hainmueller (2010) data, which carry no license of their own), used in check-methods and never in a study run. (4) For the level-check decision set only: the U.S. Department of Labor Wage and Hour Division's history of state minimum wage rates, 2014-2019, recorded by the Scout (s-mw-history) to confirm that every D20 state's binding minimum was the federal $7.25 throughout; it enters no estimator. UNIT AND SAMPLE: state x quarter; 50 states and DC (51 units; Puerto Rico and the Virgin Islands excluded); 2014Q1-2026Q1; treated unit California (06). Pools: D20 = Dube's 20 states whose binding fast-food minimum is the federal $7.25 (AL 01, GA 13, IA 19, ID 16, IN 18, KS 20, KY 21, LA 22, MS 28, NC 37, ND 38, NH 33, OK 40, PA 42, SC 45, TN 47, TX 48, UT 49, WI 55, WY 56); R50 = all 50 other units (CEM's 'rest of US', here including Alaska and Michigan, which CEMN drop for their monthly panel; our state rows have no gaps). COVID quarters 2020Q1-2021Q4 stay in the files but are used only in figures. 722515 is never used (covered chains). VARIABLES (built by prepare-state): emp_X = mean(month1_emplvl, month2_emplvl, month3_emplvl) for X in {722513, 722511, 7225, 10}; emp_nonff = emp_10 - emp_722513; sep_722513 = month3_emplvl (for the CEM cross-check); wages_722513 = total_qtrly_wages; aww_722513 = avg_wkly_wage (checked against wages / (13 * emp) to within $1); pop; sup_7225 = state 7225 row suppressed. FILES: data/derived/state_panel.csv (all quarters) and data/derived/state_panel_pre.csv (the same rows for 2014Q1-2019Q4 only; the only input of select and level-mde). Both come from one data-prep run that computes no statistic comparing areas or periods.
analysis_plan: 0a. fetch-data and 0b. prepare-data (data-prep, data-ra; done): QCEW slices and county/state panel (data/CODEBOOK.md).

0c. fetch-pop (data-prep, data-ra, code/fetch_pop.py; task dr-pop): the two Census files in data/raw/census/, manifest entries with sha256, URL, license and retrieval date; the intercensal file's totals are summed in prepare-state, not here.
0d. fetch-prop99 (data-prep, data-ra, code/fetch_prop99.py; task dr-prop99): california_prop99.csv into data/raw/synthdid/, manifest entry and license. Used only by check-methods.

0e. prepare-state (data-prep, data-ra, code/prepare_state.py; task dr-state): builds state_panel.csv and state_panel_pre.csv as in design.data. Checks: 51 units x 49 quarters, no missing 722513/722511/10 state value, the aww identity, the splice of the two population files (count of states whose July 2020 Vintage 2025 / July 2019 intercensal ratio lies outside 0.97-1.03; population only, no outcome), the population extrapolation flag, and state_panel_pre.csv = the 2014Q1-2019Q4 rows of state_panel.csv byte for byte. CODEBOOK addendum. No statistic comparing areas or periods.

0f. check-methods (data-prep, econometrician, code/test_sclib.py importing code/sclib.py; synthetic data and Prop 99 only; task e-check; before the code review). (i) Prop 99 (39 states, 1970-2000, treated from 1989; T_pre = 19, T_post = 12, N_co = 38, N_tr = 1; zeta = (1 * 12)^(1/4) sigma_hat): each estimate must round to the value Arkhangelsky et al. (2021) Table 1 prints to one decimal (claim c-sdid-prop99; notes section 9 item 9), i.e. lie in the printed value's rounding interval: DID -27.3, [-27.35, -27.25); SDID -15.6, [-15.65, -15.55); SC without intercept (zeta = 1e-6 sigma_hat, no time weights; the paper's SC) -19.6, [-19.65, -19.55). The script also prints each estimate to three decimals. sigma_hat and both penalties as design.method SDID (eq. 2.2; unit penalty zeta^2 T_pre ||omega||^2; time penalty (1e-6 sigma_hat)^2 N_co ||lambda||^2, fn 3). A miss is a bug to find, not a reason to change the algorithm. (ii) Synthetic panels with one treated unit, 20 and 50 donors and a known effect: DD/DDT closed forms equal an OLS TWFE with unit and time effects (plus unit trends for DDT), population weights included, to 1e-10; SC and SDID recover exact weights when the treated unit is a convex combination; demeaned SC equals the SDID routine with zeta = 0 and uniform time weights; the KKT conditions hold to 1e-6. (iii) Seasonal factors computed from state_panel_pre.csv equal those computed from state_panel.csv. (iv) Monte Carlo of the inference (design-r1 D1): synthetic panels with the real 2016Q1 populations of California plus D20 and of California plus R50 (population only, from state_panel_pre.csv; no outcome column read), 2014Q1-2019Q4, unit and quarter effects, California treated at B' = 2017Q2, true effect 0, errors e_jt = a_jt + u_jt with Gaussian a_jt of variance sigma_A^2 (state-level shock) and u_jt of variance sigma_B^2 pop_med/pop_j (size-related noise), each AR(1) with rho in {0, 0.5}, in three designs: pure B (sigma_A = 0), pure A (sigma_B = 0) and mixed (sigma_A = sigma_B, equal at the median state); six designs in all. Estimators: DD-POPW-E and DDT-POPW-E with both pools and SC-E and SDID-E with D20, 2,000 replications each; SC-E and SDID-E with R50, 500 replications. Pass condition, stated in the script before it runs: with SE = max(SE_s, SE_n) and t_J critical values, California's one-sided 5% test (upper and lower tails) and two-sided 5% test each reject at most 0.05 + 3*sqrt(0.05*0.95/R) in every design (R = replications). The scaled-only rates are reported next to them (expected to exceed 0.05 under pure A and mixed). A failure of the max-SE test is returned to the Designer before the design gate; it is not tuned away. (v) select.py and level_mde.py raise an error if their input contains any quarter after 2019Q4.

1. select (analysis, econometrician, code/select.py + code/sclib.py; --input data/derived/state_panel_pre.csv only; first analysis run after the design gate, run once): the 24 candidates x 6 pseudo-dates of California pseudo-ATTs (runs/select/pseudo_atts.csv); metrics rmse_<id> for every candidate, maxabs_<id>, selected (the id), selected_rmse, tie_used (0/1). All values are pre-2020 placebo numbers; the paper reports all 24.

2. level-mde (analysis, econometrician, code/level_mde.py; --input state_panel_pre.csv and runs/select/metrics.json; after the design gate and before any run that reads a post-2023Q3 outcome; data end 2019Q4): for each statistic in design.method LEVEL CHECK (selected candidate H1, H2, H3; S1 H2; S2 H2; other-pool H2), the rejection rates with SE, SE_s and SE_n over all tests, by population tercile, over the decision set L (ten most populous D20 states) and for California, with the effective number of independent draws; the critical values c_hi(0.95), c_hi(0.975), c_lo(0.05), c_lo(0.025) and the t_J and L-quantile values they came from; the Ferman-Pinto diagnostic A_hat, B_hat and SE_FP for California at each B'; diagnostic k; SE_pre, SE_s,pre, SE_n,pre; MDE_h1, MDE_h2, MDE_h3, h3_informative (MDE_h3 <= 0.04), h90_h2, and the nine H2 label probabilities under tau = 0 and tau = -0.035.

3. h1-wage (analysis, code/h1_wage.py; full panel): pooled W ATT 2024Q2-2026Q1 and the year-1 and year-2 W ATTs, SEs, the one-sided 5% test for each, dollars at the 2023Q3 California weekly wage. H1 counts against the first stage if the pooled test does not reject.

4. h2-emp (analysis, code/h2_emp.py): pooled E-or-P ATT, SE, 95% and 90% CIs, placebo estimates, percent and implied jobs (mean post California employment x (1 - exp(-tau))), MDE_h2, h90 and the label probabilities carried through from level-mde, and MDE_h2 and h90 recomputed with this run's SE (report-only; design-r1 D6). A 'decline of at least 2%' counts against the near-zero reading (Dube); 'no effect as large as 2%' or 'decline smaller than 2%' count against the about -3.5% reading (CEMN).

5. h3-years (analysis, code/h3_years.py): year-1 and year-2 employment ATTs (SDID: same omega, lambda refitted per year), the difference, its SE and 95% CI, MDE_h3 recomputed with this run's SE, and yearly and pooled elasticities (with h1-wage metrics as --input): denominator = the wage ATT with the employment fit reused, plus the refitted-weights ratio for SC and SDID (design.method DECISIONS; design-r1 D5). The H3 label is replaced by 'uninformative' if h3_informative = 0 or the recomputed MDE_h3 exceeds 0.04.
6. anticip (analysis, code/anticip.py; report-only): the employment and wage ATT over 2023Q4-2024Q1 against base 2023Q3, with the same estimator, pool and SE. No label, no test claim.

7. sec-cemn (analysis, code/sec_cemn.py; secondary S1, reported whatever the rule picks): CEM's detrended indexed DD under the 2023Q3 timing. g_t = SA ln(E_CA) - SA ln(sum of R50 employment); tau = mean over 2024Q2-2026Q1 of [g_t - g_B - (t - B)(g_B - g_{B-8})/8], i.e. CEM's endpoint 2021Q3-2023Q3 growth trend (2021Q3 kept, as CEM do); the simple (undetrended) version too. Inference as design.method INFERENCE with R50 and S1's level-mde critical values, plus CEM's placebo rank p (b+1)/(m+1). Reports S1's H2 rule label (sign and size), which enters the verdict (design-r1 D4). Report-only cross-check against print: the September-to-September fixed horizon 2023-2025 on month3 levels, R50 minus AK and MI (48 states, as CEMN), simple and detrended (two times the annual 2021-2023 trend), next to CEMN Table 3 Panel B (-2.74, -3.72).

8. sec-dube (analysis, code/sec_dube.py; secondary S2): Dube's SDID under the 2023Q3 timing: SA log(emp/pop), D20, pre 2015Q1-2023Q3 excluding C, post 2024Q2-2026Q1, the wage effect with the employment omega and lambda reused (Dube's choice), inference as design.method INFERENCE with S2's level-mde critical values. Reports S2's H2 rule label, which enters the verdict (design-r1 D4). Report-only cross-check: Dube's own timing (pre 2015Q1-2023Q4 excluding C, 2024Q1 dropped, post 2024Q2-2025Q3) next to Table 1 Panel A SDID (-0.26 [0.54], wage +6.99).

9. rob-base-2023q4 (analysis, code/robust.py base2023q4): the selected estimator and pool with Dube's base. B = 2023Q4 (fit windows end 2023Q4, DDT trend over 2022Q1-2023Q4), 2024Q1 dropped, post 2024Q2-2026Q1.

10. rob-pre-ab257 (analysis, code/robust.py preab257; literature-r1 L1): B = 2022Q2, the last quarter before AB 257 was enacted (September 2022). Fit windows end 2022Q2; 2022Q3-2024Q1 is excluded from the base, the fit and the post window; post 2024Q2-2026Q1. For DDT the trend uses the last 9 non-COVID quarters up to 2022Q2 (2018Q1-2019Q4 and 2022Q1-2022Q2), because B-8..B holds only 2 non-COVID points. This reports the base-period choice both ways (2023Q3 inside the AB 257 window, 2022Q2 before it) and also covers anticipation of AB 1228 from mid-2023 (Sosinskiy-Reich p. 42).
11. rob-pool (analysis, code/robust.py pool): the selected estimator and normalisation with the other pool (D20 <-> R50).

12. rob-7225 (analysis, code/robust.py naics7225): outcome = 7225 (all restaurants) employment. Four state 7225 rows are suppressed, all in 2024Q4 (inside the post window): Alaska, New Hampshire, Vermont and Wyoming (CODEBOOK addendum, discrepancy 2). Main number: those four donors are dropped for this run and listed, so D20 has J = 18 (NH and WY out) and R50 has J = 46; the run uses t at its own J with the selected candidate's L quantile (design.method LEVEL CHECK). Second number, same run: all donors kept and 2024Q4 dropped from every unit's post window (7-quarter post mean, year 1 = 2024Q2-2024Q3 plus 2025Q1), so donor composition cannot drive the difference. Reading: a 722513 decline with no 7225 decline points to reclassification between restaurant codes (Melo et al.) or substitution toward other restaurants, not job loss in restaurants. California's 7225 rows are not suppressed.

13. rob-final-quarters (analysis, code/robust.py final7): post window 2024Q2-2025Q4 (7 quarters, no preliminary 2026Q1 data). Shows how much the one new, preliminary quarter moves the pooled estimate.

14. plc-nonff (analysis, code/placebo_outcome.py nonff; placebo outcome): employment in all covered industries except 722513, with the selected estimator and pool. The law's direct share of this aggregate is small. Failure = a 95% CI that excludes 0: the comparison does not hold for California's aggregate labour market, and the paper qualifies the H2 label as 'not separable from a California-wide shock'. No re-specification follows.

15. plc-722511 (analysis, code/placebo_outcome.py 722511): full-service employment. Not a clean placebo (literature-r1 L2): covered chains are also coded in 722511 (Melo et al.: 7.9% of matched chain locations in Louisiana), and CEMN report wage and price spillovers to full service. A 722511 effect therefore mixes misfiled covered establishments, spillovers and restaurant-wide shocks. What it can show: a 722511 decline of similar size to H2 means the 722513 result is not specific to the limited-service code and may reflect a restaurant-wide shock. What it cannot show: a null or opposite-signed 722511 effect does not validate the design, and no 722511 result is used as a DDD comparison. Reported only.

16. event-path (analysis, code/event_path.py; report-only, for the figure): quarterly California-minus-counterfactual gaps 2014Q1-2026Q1 for the selected candidate (E-or-P and W), with real-B weights and trend and pointwise bands with SE = max(SE_s, SE_n) and the selected candidate's H2 critical values. COVID quarters are shaded and AB 257 (2022Q3) and AB 1228 (2023Q4) are marked. The pre-period gaps 2022Q1-2023Q3 are the visible check of (ii).

17. verdict (analysis, code/verdict.py; inputs the metrics of runs 2-5, 7, 8 and 9-13): H1 flag, H2 sign, size and label, H3 label or 'uninformative', elasticities or 'not computed'. Each robustness run (9-13) and each secondary (S1, S2) also reports the label the H2 rule would give, marked 'not the headline'. If S1, S2 or any of 9, 10, 11 or 13 gives a different sign category from the primary, the headline is stated as 'not robust to <check>' (design-r1 D4: the selection has about two independent draws, and S1 against S2 is the published disagreement). The abstract and the first results paragraph report the primary, S1 and S2 labels side by side, and say that an R50 or DDT winner may reflect California's shared 2014-2022 general minimum-wage ramp (T17).

18. fig-event, fig-select, fig-placebo (analysis, figures-ra, code/fig_event.py, fig_select.py, fig_placebo.py): event path; the 24 RMSEs (pre-period only); scaled placebo estimates against California's H2 estimate.
19. Claims from the metrics above, then crew.py numbers; clean rerun (crew.py rerun --setup with code/requirements.txt).
claims_plan: select: sel-candidate (text), sel-rmse, rmse of the best DD, DDT, SC and SDID candidates.

level-mde: crit-h1-hi, crit-h2-hi, crit-h2-lo, crit-h3-hi, crit-h3-lo, crit-s1, crit-s2 and the t_J and L-quantile values behind them; rej rates (all, terciles, L, CA) with SE, SE_s and SE_n; se-pre, se-s-pre, se-n-pre; fp-a-hat, fp-b-hat, fp-se; mde-h1, mde-h2, mde-h3, h90-h2; the nine H2 label probabilities under tau = 0 and -0.035.

h1-wage: h1-att, h1-se, h1-att-y1, h1-att-y2, h1-dollars. h2-emp: h2-att, h2-lo95, h2-hi95, h2-lo90, h2-hi90, h2-pct, h2-jobs. h3-years: h3-y1, h3-y2, h3-diff, h3-diff-lo, h3-diff-hi, owe-pooled, owe-y1, owe-y2.

verdict: h1-flag, h2-label, h3-label (text claims backed by the verdict run). anticip, sec-cemn, sec-dube, rob-*, plc-*: att, lo95 and hi95 each, plus the published cross-check values next to their print (marked % crew:literal for the printed side).
deviations: D1 (track rule 'cluster standard errors at the level treatment varies'): with one treated state, cluster-robust SEs are invalid (Dube p. 8; CEM p. 6; SR p. 14). Placebo-based inference with a pre-registered level check is used instead.

D2: S1 adapts CEM's monthly fixed-horizon estimator to a pooled quarterly average, which needs seasonal adjustment that CEM's September-to-September comparison does not; the faithful fixed-horizon number is reported as a cross-check.

D3: S2 uses our implementation of Arkhangelsky et al.'s Algorithm 1 (with intercept and separate penalties) and our 2014-2019 seasonal factors, not Dube's code. w35931 reports that Dube's SDID omits the intercept and uses one penalty; we cannot check his code, so the Panel A cross-check measures the combined difference.
D4: R50 keeps Alaska and Michigan, which CEMN drop; the CEM cross-check uses the 48-state pool.
threats: T1 Search moved into the rule's parameters (question-r4 F15a): the pseudo-dates, windows, COVID handling, outcome scale, tie-break, pools, inference variant rule and cutoff are all fixed above before any placebo is computed. select runs once on an input that ends in 2019Q4, and repeated selection runs remain visible in runs/.superseded. The PI and Scout know the published map (disclosed); both camps' specifications are reported as S1 and S2.

T2 The selection has little information: six overlapping pseudo-windows (about two independent draws) in calm 2016-2019, with shorter fit windows (9-14 quarters) than the real one (31). DD and DDT trend windows are alike at pseudo-dates but differ after COVID. The winner may not be the best estimator for 2024-2026. Handled by: all 24 RMSEs reported, S1 and S2 reported whatever wins and able to qualify the headline as 'not robust' (verdict; design-r1 D4), rob-pool, event-path. No re-selection.

T3 COVID: every eight-quarter pseudo-window from 2018Q3 contains COVID quarters, so all pseudo-windows end by 2019Q4 and 2020Q1-2021Q4 is excluded from every fit, base, trend and SE. The real fit windows straddle the gap, which the pseudo-dates do not mimic (T2). event-path shows the straddle.

T4 AB 257 (enacted September 2022, a possible $22 fast-food wage, stayed January 2023, replaced by AB 1228; literature-r1 L1): 2022Q3-2023Q3, including the 2023Q3 base and the end of every real fit window, falls under a pending sectoral wage law. The selection, the level check and the MDE use only 2014Q1-2019Q4, so they avoid it. The base is reported both ways: rob-pre-ab257 (base 2022Q2; 2022Q3-2024Q1 excluded from fit and base) against the primary 2023Q3. The event path marks 2022Q3.

T5 Anticipation of AB 1228 before signing (Sosinskiy-Reich p. 42: as early as July-August 2023) biases a 2023Q3 base: rob-pre-ab257 (2022Q2 base), event-path. Anticipation between signing and the effective date: the anticip estimate (report-only) and rob-base-2023q4 (Dube's base).

T6 Inference with one treated state (design-r1 D1): the population-scaled placebo SE alone assumes var(tau_j) proportional to 1/pop_j (Ferman-Pinto A = 0). State QCEW 722513 is a near-census, so state-level shocks (A > 0) are likely, and then the scaled SE understates California's SE because California is larger than every donor, while a level check pooled over all units can pass because small units under-reject. Handled by: SE = max(scaled, unscaled), conservative for the largest unit for any A, B >= 0; critical values never below t_J and widened by the over-rejection of the ten most populous policy-free D20 states (not by a pooled rate); rates reported by population tercile, for L and for California; the Ferman-Pinto A_hat, B_hat diagnostic; and a check-methods Monte Carlo with A > 0 designs. Remaining risk: variance rising with size (B < 0) or California-specific noise beyond size; L contains no unit as large as California, so its level for California is argued, not measured. Cost: wider intervals, shown by MDE_h2, h90 and the label probabilities.

T7 MDE from 2014-2019 noise may understate post-COVID noise: the real SE from h2-emp is reported next to MDE_h2, and MDE_h2, h90 and MDE_h3 are recomputed with it (the H3 rule uses the larger MDE_h3).

T8 Donor contamination: R50 states that raised their minimum wages during 2024-2026 bias the R50 estimate toward a smaller decline. D20 states have no minimum-wage change but differ economically. rob-pool and S1 versus S2 show the difference.

T9 Treated sector is wider than and different from 722513: covered chains sit in 722515 (never used) and in 722511 (Melo et al. 7.9% of chain locations in Louisiana; L2). 722511 is therefore reported as a non-clean placebo only (plc-722511) and is never a DDD control. Classification can change with the policy: rob-7225.

T10 Dilution: tau is an intent-to-treat effect on all of 722513. Melo et al. put California covered-chain employment (YTS) about one third below QCEW 722513 in 2025, an approximation from another universe; no rescaling is done. The own-wage elasticity is roughly invariant to dilution.

T11 QCEW counts jobs held in the pay period including the 12th, not hours; weekly earnings are not the hourly wage, so H1 is biased toward zero if hours fell, and lower turnover can lower counts (Dube App. B). Stated as limits; no fix.

T12 Concurrent California shocks: the general minimum wage rises (affecting uncovered 722513 and 722511 workers), SB 525 (health care, from October 2024), and California's slower population growth (per-capita candidates; Census extrapolation for 2025Q3-2026Q1 matters only if a P candidate wins). plc-nonff is the check; a failure qualifies H2.

T13 Seasonal factors are estimated on 2014-2019, the years of the pseudo-windows, which flatters every candidate's placebo RMSE about equally and flatters SE_pre and hence the MDE and h90 (design-r1 D6; the post-period recomputation in T7 is the check). Stale factors after COVID mostly average out over two full post years, except at the single Q3 base: event-path, rob-base-2023q4 (a Q4 base).
T14 Data revisions: 2026Q1 is preliminary and 2025 will be revised. The vintage is pinned by the manifest hashes; rob-final-quarters drops 2026Q1.
T15 Nominal wages: differential price changes between California and donors enter H1. Stated.

T16 Code errors: check-methods (Prop 99 against Arkhangelsky et al. Table 1, synthetic identities, Monte Carlo level), code review before any analysis run, the published cross-checks in sec-cemn and sec-dube, and a clean rerun.

T17 The pre-period is not policy-free (design-r1 D3): California's general minimum wage rose every year from July 2014 to $15 in 2022 (Wiltshire et al.), the D20 donors stayed at $7.25, and many R50 states raised theirs in 2014-2019. (i) Selection: California's pseudo-ATTs contain the relative effect of that ramp, so the rule rewards candidates that track it (a gap trend, DDT, or donors with their own increases, R50), whether or not they reproduce the AB 1228-free path after 2023, when the general minimum rose more slowly. The premise is restated accordingly (identifying_assumption), and the paper says that an R50 or DDT winner may reflect the shared ramp. (ii) Level check: R50 units treated at pseudo-dates carry their own increases, so their T values are not null draws; the critical values therefore use only L, the ten most populous D20 states (federal minimum throughout 2014-2019, s-mw-history), and rates over all units are reported as context. (iii) MDE: SE_pre uses donor placebos and is reported as a lower bound (T7). S1 and S2 can qualify the headline (verdict).
